papers.title: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Noisy Data for Fine-Grained Recognition
papers.abstract: Current approaches for fine-grained recognition do the following: First, recruit experts to annotate a dataset of images, optionally also collecting more structured data in the form of part annotations and bounding boxes. Second, train a model utilizing this data. Toward the goal of solving fine-grained recognition, we introduce an alternative approach, leveraging free, noisy data from the web and simple, generic methods of recognition. This approach has benefits in both performance and scalability. We demonstrate its efficacy on four fine-grained datasets, greatly exceeding existing state of the art without the manual collection of even a single label, and furthermore show first results at scaling to more than 10,000 fine-grained categories. Quantitatively, we achieve top-1 accuracies of 92.3% on CUB-200-2011, 85.4% on Birdsnap, 93.4% on FGVC-Aircraft, and 80.8% on Stanford Dogs without using their annotated training sets. We compare our approach to an active learning approach for expanding fine-grained datasets.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究细粒度图像识别，与FEA替代建模或生物力学设计无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper addresses fine-grained visual recognition using noisy web data, with no connection to finite element analysis, surrogate modeling, uncertainty quantification, or biomechanical design.

summary_zh.motivation: 利用免费网络噪声数据解决细粒度识别问题。
summary_zh.method: 使用简单通用识别方法，结合网络噪声数据训练。
summary_zh.result: 在四个数据集上超越现有方法，无需手工标注。
summary_zh.validation: 在CUB-200等数据集上测试分类准确率。

summary_en.motivation: To achieve fine-grained image recognition without expensive manual annotation by leveraging freely available noisy web data.
summary_en.method: Simple generic recognition models trained on noisy web images without part annotations or bounding boxes.
summary_en.result: State-of-the-art top-1 accuracies on four fine-grained datasets, e.g., 92.3% on CUB-200-2011.
summary_en.validation: Tested on standard fine-grained benchmarks (CUB-200, Birdsnap, FGVC-Aircraft, Stanford Dogs).

papers.title: The Variational Gaussian Process
papers.abstract: Variational inference is a powerful tool for approximate inference, and it has been recently applied for representation learning with deep generative models. We develop the variational Gaussian process (VGP), a Bayesian nonparametric variational family, which adapts its shape to match complex posterior distributions. The VGP generates approximate posterior samples by generating latent inputs and warping them through random non-linear mappings; the distribution over random mappings is learned during inference, enabling the transformed outputs to adapt to varying complexity. We prove a universal approximation theorem for the VGP, demonstrating its representative power for learning any model. For inference we present a variational objective inspired by auto-encoders and perform black box inference over a wide class of models. The VGP achieves new state-of-the-art results for unsupervised learning, inferring models such as the deep latent Gaussian model and the recently proposed DRAW.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文涉及变分推断和高斯过程，但未应用于有限元代理模型或生物力学问题。
llm.why_not_core: No application to FEA surrogate modelling, no constraint handling, no uncertainty quantification for simulations, no biomechanics or implant design context.

summary_zh.motivation: 开发能适应复杂后验分布的贝叶斯非参数变分族。
summary_zh.method: 通过生成潜在输入并通过随机非线性映射扭曲它们来构造变分高斯过程。
summary_zh.result: 在无监督学习任务上达到最先进水平，并证明了通用近似定理。
summary_zh.validation: 在深度潜高斯模型和DRAW等生成模型上进行了数值实验验证。

summary_en.motivation: To develop a Bayesian nonparametric variational family that can adapt its shape to match complex posterior distributions.
summary_en.method: The variational Gaussian process (VGP) generates approximate posterior samples by warping latent inputs through random nonlinear mappings learned during inference.
summary_en.result: The VGP achieves state-of-the-art results on unsupervised learning tasks and is accompanied by a universal approximation theorem.
summary_en.validation: Validation is performed through numerical experiments on deep latent Gaussian models and the DRAW generative model.

papers.title: Probability and heritability estimates on primary osteoarthritis of the hip leading to total hip arthroplasty: a nationwide population based follow-up study in Danish twins
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Primary hip osteoarthritis, radiographic as well as symptomatic, is highly associated with increasing age in both genders. However, little is known about the mechanisms behind this, in particular if this increase is caused by genetic factors. This study examined the risk and heritability of primary osteoarthritis of the hip leading to a total hip arthroplasty, and if this heritability increased with increasing age. METHODS: In a nationwide population-based follow-up study 118,788 twins from the Danish Twin Register and 90,007 individuals from the Danish Hip Arthroplasty Register for the period 1995 to 2010 were examined. Our main outcomes were the cumulative incidence, proband-wise concordance and heritability on age, within-pair correlations in monozygotic and dizygotic twin pairs, and the genetic and environmental influence estimated in models taking into account that individuals may not have had a total hip arthroplasty at the time of follow-up. RESULTS: There were 94,063 twins eligible for analyses, comprising 835 cases of 36 concordant and 763 discordant twin pairs. The probability increased particularly from 50 years of age. After sex and age adjustment a significant additive genetic component of 47% (12:79), a shared environmental component of 21% (2:76) and a unique environment component of 32% (21:41) accounted for the variation in population liability to total hip arthroplasty. The sex-adjusted proband-wise concordance and heritability on age indicated an increasing age-associated genetic influence onwards from 60 years of age. CONCLUSION: The cumulative incidence in primary hip osteoarthritis leading to total hip arthroplasty increases in particular after the age of 50 years in both genders. Family factors of genes and shared environment are highly significant and account for 68% of the variation in the population liability to total hip arthroplasty; however, the genetic influence increases significantly from 60 years of age onwards.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究髋关节骨关节炎的遗传度，与髋植入物生物力学分析无直接关联。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not quantify proximal femur stress/strain, does not report micromotion with contact modeling, is not patient-specific FE, and does not compare intact vs implanted femur mechanics; it provides no usable boundary conditions for FE work.

summary_zh.motivation: 探讨原发性髋骨关节炎导致全髋置换术的风险和遗传度。
summary_zh.method: 基于丹麦双胞胎和髋关节置换登记处数据进行随访和遗传模型分析。
summary_zh.result: 50岁后风险显著增加，遗传因素解释47%的变异。
summary_zh.validation: 通过人群统计学模型和双胞胎一致性分析验证。

summary_en.motivation: To assess the risk and heritability of primary hip osteoarthritis leading to total hip arthroplasty and whether genetic influence increases with age.
summary_en.method: A nationwide population-based follow-up study utilizing Danish Twin Register and Hip Arthroplasty Register data, with heritability estimation via structural equation modeling.
summary_en.result: The cumulative incidence rises markedly after age 50; additive genetics account for 47% of liability, with shared environment contributing 21% and unique environment 32%.
summary_en.validation: Proband-wise concordance and age-stratified heritability analysis within monozygotic and dizygotic twin pairs.
